definitions.explanation: the state of things overlapping, piling up, or being layered on top of each other
multiple events or circumstances happening at the same time or in succession

examples.japanese: {色|いろ}の{重|かさ}なりが{美|うつく}しい。
examples.english: The overlap of colors is beautiful.

examples.japanese: {布|ぬの}の{重|かさ}なりで{厚|あつ}みが{出|で}た。
examples.english: The layers of fabric created thickness.

examples.japanese: {屋根|やね}の{瓦|かわら}の{重|かさ}なりが{独特|どくとく}な{模様|もよう}を{作|つく}っている。
examples.english: The overlapping of the roof tiles creates a unique pattern.

examples.japanese: {不幸|ふこう}の{重|かさ}なりに{疲|つか}れた。
examples.english: I was worn out by the series of misfortunes.

examples.japanese: {偶然|ぐうぜん}の{重|かさ}なりで{再会|さいかい}した。
examples.english: We met again through a series of coincidences.

examples.japanese: {小|ちい}さなミスの{重|かさ}なりが{大|おお}きな{事故|じこ}につながることがある。
examples.english: An accumulation of small mistakes can lead to a major accident.

notes:
Noun form of the verb {重|かさ}なる (to overlap, to pile up). Describes either the physical state of things being layered or stacked, or the abstract idea of events or circumstances occurring one after another.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {偶然|ぐうぜん}の{重|かさ}なり: series of coincidences
- {不幸|ふこう}の{重|かさ}なり: string of misfortunes
- {色|いろ}の{重|かさ}なり: overlap of colors
- {予定|よてい}の{重|かさ}なり: scheduling conflict

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {重複|ちょうふく}: duplication — emphasizes redundancy or repetition, often of data or items
- {積|つ}み{重|かさ}ね: accumulation — emphasizes effort or deliberate building up over time
- {一致|いっち}: coincidence/match — emphasizes exact agreement rather than layering
